review: 1:1–1:2 הַגִּישׁוּ … שֶׁבַח / וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה חַיֶּבֶת — the Arabic قَدِّمُوا … سُبْحًا وَسُجُودًا قَدْ وَجَب uses two imperatives of obligation; Hebrew keeps the imperative and renders the obligation as a predicate ('worship is due').
1:4 נֹשֵׂא בַעֲדֵנוּ חֵמָה — 'bearing wrath on our behalf'; the Arabic حَامِلًا عَنَّا الْغَضَب is the same phrase as hymn 56's cup, kept without the noun 'cup' because the line is already full.

3:1–3:2 מֵת בַּעֲדֵנוּ בְּעוֹד / כֻּלָּנוּ מֵתִים בַּחֵטְא — Romans 5:8 (בְּעוֹד שֶׁהָיִינוּ חַטָּאִים); the Arabic حِينَ كُنَّا … أَمْوَاتًا خُطَاه is that verse, and Hebrew keeps בְּעוֹד as its temporal marker.
4:2 מִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת — 'within the veil' (Heb 6:19, מִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת); the Arabic دَاخِلَ الْحِجَاب is that phrase, and the doubled preposition is the biblical idiom.
5:4 וְגַדְּלוּ אֶת־אִישְׁכֶם — 'and magnify His person'; the Arabic وَلْنُعَظِّمْ شَخْصَهُ is 'let us magnify His person', and אִישׁ is used in the biblical sense of 'person' rather than 'man'.
